token_rule: prompt tokens of CohereLabs/tiny-aya-global's tokenizer without special tokens, at most 1350 (round 5's rule; the chat template adds about 60 and the run-time limit is 1536); candidates over the limit are refused before selection

chat_template_lengths.note: r4lib renders every prompt with apply_chat_template (no system turn) and a 1536-token limit; this template adds about 365 tokens, not the 60 that round 5's comment assumes, so a prompt near 1350 tokens would not fit; no new row comes near that. A system prompt added later (in-the-wild system templates are 40 to 900 tokens) adds to this.

exam_b_hash_definition: sha256 of the newline-joined sorted '<set>|<id>' keys of all xb_ rows (round 5's frozen_ids_sha256 definition); the _and_text variant appends '|sha1(text)'

overlap_checks.earlier_rows: 18918 rows of runs_private/round5/sets.jsonl (fit, development and frozen) + 1900 round 4 frozen rows + 9 ids round 5 dropped before generation
overlap_checks.question_reuse: xb_itw_h reuses the harmful questions of round 5's frozen in-the-wild slice by design (never in a fit); every template is new
overlap_checks.near_duplicate_rule: character 3-gram Jaccard of normalised text >= 0.85, computed exactly (round 5's r5_sets.py rule; CuratorKIT's threshold and n-gram without the MinHash estimate), against every earlier row and every new development row
overlap_checks.how: every candidate is checked before it is accepted (refused candidates are listed with the first earlier row they match), then every finished exam row is checked again; rows found at the second check are dropped (an in-the-wild template or a MultiJail request as a whole)

A_aya_redteaming.rule: each language split's prompts (duplicates inside a split kept once) split by sha1(normalised text) mod 5: 0 is development, the rest exam. Development xd_art_<lg>: 60 per unseen language (fil, fr, hi, ru, sr, es). Exam xb_art_<lg>: 150 per unseen language, 100 each for ar and en (languages the read has seen; reference). Candidates in the order sha1('r6|art-<lg>|<row index>'); id art-<lg>-<row index in the split>; harm_category kept as stored (a JSON list as text).
A_aya_redteaming.note: a prompt can carry several harm categories, so the category counts can sum to more than the set size; the development side of ar and en is left unused

B_aya_unseen_languages.rule: round 5's Aya rule (language code and name match, original annotations then re-annotations, 15 to 300 characters, unique normalised text, not equal to an earlier row, Aya rows used earlier excluded by index and text); split by sha1(normalised text) mod 5 == 0 development (40 per language), the rest exam (60); candidates in the order sha1('r6|ayab-<lg>|<row index>'); id ayab-<lg>-<row index in the train split>

xb_wj_h.rule: eval-split adversarial_harmful rows whose index no earlier set used (rounds 3 and 4 dev and frozen, round 5 wj5_h_frz); order sha1('r6|wjh|<index>'); id wj-<eval index>

xb_wj_b.rule: round 5's wj5_b_frz rule (train-split adversarial_benign, vanilla request in round 4's frozen partition sha1(norm(vanilla)) mod 10 >= 8, index not used before, text not equal to any earlier row nor to an eval-split row, at most 1350 tokens) plus two additions: the row's vanilla request (round 4's vanilla_hash) is behind no earlier row (round 4 rows' vanilla_hash, and the vanilla of every earlier wjtr- and aug-wjv- row), and no two new rows share a vanilla request. Order sha1('r6|wjb|<index>'); id wjtr-<train index>
xb_wj_b.why_round5_rule_still_has_candidates: round 5 scanned a seeded sample of 80,000 train rows and stopped at 350 accepted rows; the rule's pool was not exhausted

D_in_the_wild.rule: round 5's template rule (unique normalised templates, 40 to 900 tokens, community id as the group, templates without one grouped by their own hash, at most 12 templates per group; the cap counts the 150 exam and the 40 system templates together). Excluded: any template an earlier row used (by index, including the template round 5 dropped) and any template whose 3-gram Jaccard with a used template or with an already picked new template is 0.85 or more (treated as the same template). Not split (all exam). Order sha1('r6|itw|<index>'). Each exam template: 2 harmful questions = the first 2 of round 5's frozen in-the-wild questions in the order sha1('r6|itwq-<template>|<pid>-<qid>') (question reuse is intended: those questions were never in a fit), and 1 fresh Alpaca instruction (round 5's in-the-wild rule: no input, 20 to 140 characters; never used before; each template gets a different one). Fill as in round 5 (placeholder if the template has one, else appended). A template is refused whole if any of its 3 rows fails a check. Ids itw-<template>::q<pid>-<qid> and itw-<template>::a<alpaca index>.

question_reuse.source: questions of round 5's frozen in-the-wild slice (itw_h_frz), never in a fit

system_templates.note: not prompts and not part of exam B; 40 further unused eligible templates, disjoint from the 150 and not near-duplicates of them, for use as system prompts

E_multijail.rule: every request whose id no earlier row used, in all 10 languages; a request is refused whole (all 10 languages) if any of its language rows equals an earlier or new row or near-duplicates an earlier row, so every xb_mj_<lg> set holds the same requests; two languages of one request may share a text. Id mj-<request>-<lg>

E_aya_multijail_languages.rule: round 5's Aya rule and language names (see B); only the exam side of round 5's split (sha1(normalised text) mod 5 != 0) so the development side stays for later; Aya rows used earlier excluded by index and text; 40 per language in the order sha1('r6|aya-<lg>|<row index>'); id aya-<row index> as in round 5

F_orbench.rule: rows whose index no earlier row used (orb- and orb-fz- ids) and whose normalised text equals no earlier row (round 5's rule), unique; order sha1('r6|orb|<index>'); id orb-<index>

F_alpaca.rule: round 5's alp5_frz rule (no input field, 20 to 200 characters, normalised text equal to no earlier row); Alpaca rows used earlier (alp-, alp-fz-, sfx-al and in-the-wild a-ids) excluded by index and text; one fixed order sha1('r6|alp|<index>') shared with D, whose instructions are skipped here; id alp-<index>

format_requests.rule: exam: 40 each from xb_wj_h and xb_mj_en (harm 1), xb_orb, xb_alp and xb_wj_b (harm 0; 40 more xb_alp if xb_wj_b were missing), first in the order sha1('r6|fmt-<set>|<id>'). dev: the 200 requests of round 5's format tests (results/round5/robust/suites.json, ids), listed again so the file is complete; harm from that file's groups. fit: 100 harmful (50 trfit_h, 50 harmful_fit) and 100 harmless (34 trfit_b, 33 benign_fit, 33 orbench_hard_fit) round 5 fit rows, first in the order sha1('r6|fmtfit-<set>|<id>'), none of them among the 200 dev requests.
